structure.heading: Key Driver Insights, Demographic Hotspots, and Prioritised 90-Day People Action Plan
text_content: **Key Driver Insights, Demographic Hotspots, and Prioritised 90-Day People Action Plan**

Key driver analysis identifies Manager Effectiveness as the top driver of engagement, with a Pearson correlation of 0.62 to overlal engagement in FY2025. This strong relationship indicates that improvements in management capability are likely to produce measurable changes in workforce motivation and retention across business units. Recommended near-term interventions include a mandatory manager development curriculum (six modules), quarterly 360-degree feedback, and performance objectives tied to team engagement. By targeting a conservative 3–5 percentage-point uplift in engagement within 12 months, leaders can expect corresponding reductions in turnover and improvements in productivity metrics and outcomes.

Demographic analysis identifies a hotspot in Operations: frontline employees recorded an engagement score of 64 out of 100 in FY2025, signaling below-target sentiment in core delivery teams. This cohort requires prioritized listening and operational interventions because frontilne performance directly affects customer satisfaction and safety metrics. Immediate actions include targeted focus groups by 30 June 2025, weekly pulse surveys for Operations for the remainder of FY2025, and leadership huddles every two weeks. Expected outcomes: a 5-point improvement in quraterly pulse scores and a 10% reduction in SLA breaches tied to staffing by Q3 FY2025.

Priority action plan (90 days) targets employees with tenure under 12 months, who scored 61 out of 100 in FY2025. Owned by People & Culture with sponsorship from HR Business aPrtners and Operations leaders, the sprint runs 1 June–29 August 2025. Key actions:
- Day 0–30: enhanced onboarding and weekly manager check-ins
- Day 31–60: buddy program and role-clarity workshops
- Day 61–90: career-path conversations and early-retention incentievs
Measurements: raise new-hire engagement to 68+ within 90 days, reduce firs-tyear attrition by 8% within 12 months, and deliver weekly dashboards to the executive sponsor.

structure.heading: FY2025 Enterprise Engagement Scorecard and Year-on-Year Trend Summary
text_content: **FY2025 Enterprise Engagement Scorecard and Year-on-Year Trend Summary**

The FY2025 enterprise engagement assessment produced an overall engagement score of 72 out of 100, reflecting the aggregate response profile across all business units. The survey closed on 2025-03-15 and was administered under the governance of the People & Culture function in partnership with the Executive Leadership Team. Compared with the FY2024 overall engagement score of 69 out of 100, the FY2025 result represents an absolute increase of 3 points and a relative improvement of approximately 4.35% year-on-year, signalling a positive shift.

The FY2025 score is presented on the enterprise engagement scorecard alongside predefined performance bands to aid interpretation. For governance purposes, the organisation applies the following thresholds: 80–100 = High engagement (performing), 70–79 = Moderate engagement (targeted improvement), 0–69 = Low engagement (priority intervention). With a score of 72, the enterprise falls within the Moderate engagement band. This classification guides escalation, resourcing, and measurement cadence and will inform quarterly progress reviews by the People & Culture analytics team and the Executive Leadership Team regularly.

Following the survey close on 2025-03-15, the scorecard and summary findings will be presented to key stakeholders in a staged communications plan. The Executive Leadership Team will receive a consolidated briefing within two weeks of closure, followed by town-hall level summaries to be delivered by business unit leaders within 30 days. Reporting materials will include the FY2025 score (72), the FY2024 comparator (69), directional commentary, and recommended governance actions so that engagement metrics are incorporated into FY2026 budgeting and workforce planning cycles thereafter.

To track progress against the FY2025 baseline of 72, the People & Culture metrics framework establishes quarterly checkpoints, target milestones, and executive accountabilities. Primary KPIs will include overall engagement score, pulse response rates, and improvement in targeted intervention bands, with a FY2026 aspirational target to reach 75 enterprise-wide. Monitoring will use the enterprise scorecard, standardised dashboards, and quarterly score trend reports to the Audit and Risk Committee. Resourcing decisions and performance incentives will be aligned to measurable uplift over consecutive quarters and timelines.
